text:
ella: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing an Async Slab Splitter + Preemptive Prefetch Controller to reduce long-tail fragmentation on multi-tenant GPUs. TL;DR: when slab free fraction < threshold we background-split large slabs into smaller ones and emit prefetch hints for host-staged pages likely to be used soon.

raj: Sketch? Where does this live — runtime or allocator? Also cross-node / NUMA concerns.

ella: Runtime-level component that hooks into the allocator free lists. Pluggable policy module. Splitter runs on a low-priority worker thread, issues split ops via allocator API, and signals the prefetch controller with candidate page ranges. Prefetch controller uses existing page-migration API to warm host staging pools.

sophia: Concern: prefetch increases host residency and can blow commit for busy tenants. We need soft quotas + backpressure. Suggest token-bucket per-tenant + prefetch-throttle when host_residency > target.

kevin: Agree on backpressure. Also concurrency: splitter must be idempotent — avoid races where two splitters operate on same slab; use CAS on slab header or allocator-level epoch.

ella: Draft config snippet (pseudo):
```
async_splitter:
  enabled: true
  min_free_pct: 8        # start splitting if free fraction drops below this
  split_to_size: [1048576, 262144, 65536]  # bytes -> 1MB, 256KB, 64KB
prefetch:
  window_ms: 1200
  max_outstanding: 8
  tenant_tokens: 2000  # soft budget for prefetch pages
```

raj: Nice. How do we measure win? heatmap of fragmentation + fragment_ratio per tenant + alloc tail latency (99p). Also track split ops/sec.

sophia: Proposed metrics: slab_split_ops, slab_split_failures, prefetch_requests, prefetch_hits, prefetch_backpressure_events, host_residency_delta, alloc_tail_99p_latency. Correlate with token spend by tenant.

kevin: Rollout plan thoughts: feature-gated + canary in Dedicated first. Need a test harness: synthetic churn (small allocs + frees) + mixture with intermittent big allocations to validate fragmentation regressions. Add unit tests for concurrent split.

offload-bot: offload-bot: scheduled job started: run-perf-suite/frag-heatmap-canary — ETA ~2h :hourglass: (will post artifacts)

ella: One more API note: allocator should expose on_split_complete(slab_id, new_sublab_ids[]) callback so runtime metadata and accounting stay consistent. Also add split_abort(reason) hooks for cleanup.

raj: For cross-node NUMA: prefer splitting only when slab affinity == requesting NUMA node. If we must move pages we should treat migration cost explicitly and gate by migration_budget.

sophia: Also think about evals: run live traffic replay and measure end-to-end tail latency and token cost delta. If prefetch increases cost by X% but reduces tail by Y ms, we need threshold rules. Maybe a simple RL score later but not now.

kevin: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with diagrams (split state machine), API signatures, race conditions and a canary rollout checklist. Will include perf harness and telemetry dashboards to validate.

ella: :thumbsup: Thanks — if no objections I'll drop the draft under docs/architecture and ping eng-sre + product for canary gating.
